title: Rollforward Safety Net Validator: staged validation harness for upgrade rollforwards
creator: Aisha Gupta
description:
Summary: Implement a Rollforward Safety Net Validator (RSNV) — a staged validation harness that runs a curated, low-latency battery of checks during upgrade window to decide whether a rollforward is safe. The RSNV complements existing release gates by focusing on 'rollforward' scenarios (deploying a newer runtime/model variant to live clusters) and providing explicit pass/fail signals plus root-cause hints when signals are borderline.

Goals:
- Surface actionable, automated pass/fail decisions for rollforward workflows (can be used by orchestrator to permit automated rollforwards).
- Run within tight time budget (target total wall time <= 6 minutes per candidate) so it can be invoked synchronously as part of controlled rollouts.
- Provide multi-signal synthesis: perf percentiles, error budgets, golden prompt evals, KV-cache warmup behavior, and resource telemetry.
- Produce a human-readable verdict with prioritized troubleshooting hints and links to artifacts.

Scope / What this ticket delivers:
- A harness that executes a 6-minute validation run against a staging copy of the serving cluster (shadow traffic replay + synthetic traces).
- Signal definitions & thresholds for immediate rollforward gating: 99th latency delta, p95 latency delta, CPU/GPU utilization spike, token-per-cost regression, and eval-quality drift on a curated testset.
- A verdict synthesizer that combines signals into one of: PASS / PASS-WITH-WARNINGS / FAIL. WARNINGS include clear next steps.
- Integration points: orchestration API hook (POST /v1/rollout/validate), Console UI endpoint to display verdicts and time-series links, and GitHub PR annotation for release commits.

Acceptance criteria:
1) RSNV returns verdict within 6 minutes for the standard validation profile (staging footprint: 4 x T4-like instances).
2) Perf guard rails: >= 3% increase in p99 latency or >= 5% increase in p95 latency relative to baseline triggers FAIL, with configurable thresholds per release channel.
3) Quality guard rails: average BLEU/ROUGE/Embedding-similarity fall below configured floor or >2% of prompts flip from expected output class -> FAIL.
4) KV-cache sanity: first-request generation latency and steady-state token throughput match baseline within thresholds; cache-warmup artefacts logged.
5) Telemetry and links: verdict includes direct links to Console traces, cost breakdown, and failing example prompts in Drive.
6) Orchestrator integration: when RSNV returns FAIL, automated rollforward is blocked; PASS allows rollforward to continue.

Planned steps / implementation notes:
- Phase A: signal spec & runner (this ticket)
  - Implement a lightweight runner service that accepts a validation profile and candidate release tag.
  - Runner executes: (1) traffic replay component (recorded 5-minute golden trace), (2) synthetic prompt set (200 prompts with guarded ROI), and (3) perf probes at target concurrency.
  - Collect metrics from agent endpoints (latency histograms, error rates, GPU mem/SM utilization) and from console APIs.
  - Implement a verdict synthesizer using weighted rules (configurable per project/channel).
- Phase B: orchestration + UI (follow-up tickets)
  - Expose REST hook for orchestrator, add dashboard card in Console, annotate PRs with pass/fail.
- Implementation constraints:
  - Runner must run in an isolated namespace with read-only access to production traffic replay artifacts.
  - Costs: keep GPU usage minimal; we will reuse smaller inference instances and replay low-QPS golden trace.
  - Must not mutate customer data or routing rules.

Telemetry & thresholds (initial):
- p95 latency delta threshold: 5% (FAIL if candidate > baseline * 1.05)
- p99 latency delta threshold: 3% (FAIL if candidate > baseline * 1.03)
- Error rate threshold: absolute increase > 0.1% OR relative > 20% -> FAIL
- Cost-per-token regression: > 7% -> PASS-WITH-WARNINGS
- Eval similarity drop (embedding cosine average): decrease > 0.02 -> FAIL

Test plan:
- Unit tests for verdict synthesizer rules and threshold parsing.
- Integration test against a local min-cluster using recorded trace (CI job).
- Canary day run: schedule RSNV on next minor runtime release on staging clusters; verify verdicts align with manual postmortem.

Open trade-offs & discussion notes:
- Duration vs signal fidelity: We target 6 minutes to keep rollouts fast; this limits sample sizes and may increase false positives. We mitigate with a PASS-WITH-WARNINGS outcome and link to a longer validation profile.
- Deterministic vs statistical thresholds: initial rollout uses fixed percentage thresholds; in future we may move to Bayesian/relative-drift detectors.
- Replay fidelity: recorded traces omit some tail-user paths. We will include targeted synthetic scenarios for rare but high-cost patterns.

Links to artifacts / references:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RELEASE/pages/RSNV+Design+Spec
- Recording bucket for golden traces: gs://redwood-release-artifacts/golden-traces/2026-q1/
- GitHub draft for runner: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-tools/pull/214
- Console card mock: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1exampleMock/view

Current progress / status updates:
- 2026-03-01: Signal spec drafted and reviewed with Applied ML (Li Wei). Feedback: tighten embedding similarity metric to use cross-check of two encoders.
- 2026-03-03: Traffic replay component PoC done (local), runner scaffolding created (branch: feature/rsnv-runner).
- 2026-03-05: Initial verdict synthesizer implemented; unit tests for rules added.

Blockers / risks:
- Need access to sanitized production traces for better fidelity; security team approval pending (SEC-3091).
- Cost approvals for staging GPUs for nightly validation windows.

Next steps (short term):
- Secure trace access and finalize replay infra (owner: Marco).
- Wire runner to orchestration API stub and add basic Console annotation (owner: Aisha).
- Run first end-to-end validation against runtime-1.20-beta in staging and capture verdicts.

Owner notes: This ticket focuses on the short, actionable validation loop for rollforward decisions. Longer-running suites (full perf regressions, extended evals) will remain separate and triggered asynchronously. The RSNV should act as the quick safety net for automated rollforwards and also provide high-signal hints to engineers when manual investigation is needed.
